extraction.name: SeamlessM4T
extraction.description: SeamlessM4T is a massively multilingual and multimodal machine translation model that supports speech-to-speech translation, speech-to-text translation, text-to-speech translation, text-to-text translation, and automatic speech recognition for up to 100 languages.
extraction.creator: Meta AI Research
extraction.citeAs: Seamless Communication et al., SeamlessM4T: Massively Multilingual & Multimodal Machine Translation, arXiv:2308.11596v3, 2023
extraction.rai:dataCollection: We used 1 million hours of open speech audio data for self-supervised speech representations with w2v-BERT 2.0. We created a multimodal corpus of automatically aligned speech translations (SeamlessAlign) of more than 470,000 hours. We combined a filtered subset of this corpus with human-labeled and pseudo-labeled data, totaling 406,000 hours.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: We start with 4 million hours of raw audio originating from a publicly available repository of crawled web data. On the text side, we rely entirely on the same dataset deployed in NLLB. The same data sources, cleaning, and filtering steps are used and run at scale with our Stopes library.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: We applied a series of pre-processing steps to curate and improve the overall speech quality. Firstly, we deduplicated the audio file URLs found in the repository, downloaded the audio files, and resampled at 16KHz. Subsequently, we filtered out the non-speech data with a bespoke audio event detection (AED) model.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: When using human-labeled data, we removed special tokens such as <silence> and <no-speech> from the verbatim transcriptions. We additionally perform length filtering to remove examples exceeding a maximum text length of 100 sub-word tokens and pairs with a skewed text-to-audio length ratio that exceeds 5 sub-words per second. We perform additional filtering on the combined pool of primary and mined data. Following NLLB Team et al. [2022], we implemented a toxicity filter. This removes pairs that have toxicity imbalance. We set the imbalance threshold at 1. In addition, we also applied a length filter. We removed pairs in which the utterance is shorter than 0.1 seconds or longer than 50 seconds. We also removed pairs in which the text is longer than 250 sub-words. Lastly, we removed pairs in which the text contains more than 20% of emojis, more than 50% of punctuations, or more than 50% of spaces.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For S2ST, we used TTS models to convert text from speech-to-text datasets into synthetic speech. This synthetic speech is in turn converted into units using the previously described unit extraction pipeline. To overcome these challenges, we circumvented the need for synthesizing speech and trained multilingual text-to-unit (T2U) models on all the 36 target speech languages. These models can directly convert the text into target discrete units and can be trained on ASR datasets that are readily available. To remove outlier samples from our paired data, we filtered based on the number of seconds of audio generated per text token length ratio, discarding any pair with a ratio exceeding 0.5.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 annotators examined each source-target audio pair (or audio-text pair) and evaluated the item for semantic similarity using the XSTS protocol. In cases where the 3 annotators had a disagreement of score values of 2 or more, 2 additional annotators evaluated the same item again, bringing the total to 5 evaluator scores for those items.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: We used NLLB-200-3.3B to generate pseudo-labels with the recommended decoding options from NLLB Team et al. [2022]. We used an open Voice Activity Detection (VAD) model to split audio files into shorter segments. We trained our own LID model, following the ECAPA-TDNN architecture. We used XLS-R-1B for continuous speech representations. We applied a k-means algorithm on these representations to estimate K cluster centroids. We used the HiFi-GAN vocoder equipped with language embedding to model the language-specific acoustic information. We used Whisper-Large-v2 and Whisper-Medium as the underlying ASR model for ASR-BLEU. We used ETOX for toxicity detection.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The training data used for model development were mined from various publicly available sources on the web. Although we invested heavily in data cleaning, personally identifiable information may not be entirely eliminated.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The downstream applications that SeamlessM4T supports could allow on-demand access to world-readiness by streamlining multilingual exchange across various contexts. SeamlessM4T's focus on multimodality could make a meaningful difference in augmenting the world-readiness of those with accessibility needs and those whose languages contain multiple writing systems. While quality translation could improve world readiness and information access for many in these communities, such access could also make groups with lower levels of digital literacy more vulnerable to misinformation or online scams.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: We evaluated for gender bias on the Multilingual HolisticBias datasets and found that SeamlessM4T overgeneralizes to masculine forms when translating from neutral terms (with an average preference of ~10%) while showing a lack of robustness when varying gender by an amount of ~3%. For these conditions, SeamlessM4T achieved comparable results to state-of-the-art models. We find that masculine representation is predominant in most of the datasets. Extremely low representations of gender are found in EuroParl, Fleurs, and Flores datasets.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: SeamlessM4T is a research model and is not released for production deployment. SeamlessM4T is trained on general domain data and is not intended to be used with domain specific inputs, such as medical domain or legal domain. The model is not intended to be used for long-form translation. The model was trained on short text and speech inputs, therefore translating longer sequences might result in quality degradation. SeamlessM4T translations can not be used as certified translations. Although we did our best to optimize for translation quality, toxic, biased, or false outputs produced by the model could remain. The use of toxicity lists with ETOX for added toxicity detection shares the same limitations with other word list-based detection techniques. The use of noun lists for the detection of linguistic gender imbalance in large datasets shares all of the limitations of word list-based techniques previously stated.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: SeamlessM4T is a multilingual and multimodal translation model primarily intended for research in speech and text translation. It allows for: ASR (Automatic speech recognition for 96 languages), S2ST (Speech-to-Speech translation from 100 source speech languages into 35 target speech languages), S2TT (Speech-to-text translation from 100 source speech languages into 95 target text languages), T2ST (Text-to-Speech translation from 95 source text languages into 35 target speech languages), T2TT (Text-to-text translation from 95 source text languages into 95 target text languages), TTS (Text-to-speech synthesis for 36 languages). Primary users are researchers and machine translation (speech and text) research community.
